Its only call site is state-tree.ts:216 in `removesOnly`. A search finds no other use, and the base has no such helper. The helper should be inlined, so the rule is violated as claimed.

evidence.snippet:
Any other unknown entry refuses every call on every changeset. Examples: an `index.json` at the root; `changesets/Bad Name!/x.json`, under a directory no changeset could be named; `changesets` itself as a file rather than a folder.

Each refusal is a `RecordError` with the code `unknownFile` that names the entry, and `melian doctor` names every unknown entry for a writer to remove.

### What the refusal still promises

Melian judges every entry of the tree it fetched before it answers a call or builds a commit, so a refused call returns no record, not even the known ones beside the stray, and pushes nothing. That is what "before a byte is read in part or pushed over" now means: no call answers from a tree it has judged in part, and no push replaces a tree it has not judged whole.

lowered.reason: The harm is narrow. `removesOnly` refuses any commit that does anything but delete whole, clean, merged changeset folders. Every other root entry and every kept folder is carried over by object ID, so a stray is neither rewritten nor read. Base already accepts carrying a stray unchanged in other writes. Retire only shrinks the tip and does not answer from a partly judged tree.

verification.reason: The code does what the claim says. `retire()` calls `StateTree.folders`, which reads only the top level of `changesets/`. It never calls `refuse()` and never judges the whole tree. A root `index.json` or a `changesets/Bad Name!/` entry is dropped silently in `folders()`, so `retire` still builds and pushes a commit, and `removesOnly` does not look for strays. The base decision says "Any other unknown entry refuses every call on every changeset" and "no push replaces a tree it has not judged whole". Its reason, that a tree holding an unknown entry stops all work until a writer clears it, still holds. The head decision (2026-11-21) amends only "what a tip past a limit refuses". It never exempts retirement from refusing on a root-level or `changesets/`-level stray. The retire tests assert the opposite behaviour. Retire is new since base, so the "every call" list there names only the five older calls. That is a point against the claim, but the sentence's reach is "every call", and the push-over-unjudged-tree clause applies to retire directly.

evidence.snippet: Solution: Pi's storage is working state and stays local, SQLite in a clone and thrown away on a runner. Hosts share the record through core's `RecordStore` port: add a batch of immutable records, list a changeset's records, fresh or not at all, one compare-and-set cell per changeset for the publication lease, and dispose. The contract assumes no ordering, history, transaction, secrecy or writer identity, so git, a directory, an object store or a database can meet it, and every adapter runs one conformance suite. The git adapter keeps `melian/state`, commits built with git's plumbing and never a checkout, `--force-with-lease` with backoff, and a wall-clock deadline; a record is a plain JSON file, and one commit holds a batch. Every store refuses a record past core's `recordLimit`, 4 MiB, and the relay takes a file up to that limit and a batch up to twice it. A guardrails record that would pass the limit keeps every finding's ID, severity and place. It leaves out the detail of its last findings in ID order, as [issue #605](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/605) asked. A notice's headline names the kind of each switch-off, such as changed npm scripts, so a trimmed notice still says it. Every other check's record gets the same budget, so Biome, tsc, Enola or mutation findings past it are trimmed alike. A record that cannot fit even so fails its check, and the review reads not reviewed, by the maintainer's ruling that [the decision](decisions/2026-11-20-guardrails-record-fits-the-store.md) records. The budget measures a check's own findings, not the record the review exports, so an exported record can still pass the limit, as the decision's known limits say, until [issue #626](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/626) lands. It builds commits in a bare repository of its own beside the clone, `records.git`, and fetches the branch's whole history into it. A file Melian did not write refuses work on the changeset whose folder holds it, or all work when it sits anywhere else, by [the am [cut at 2 KiB]

On 2026-11-22 the coordinator directed, in its own session, that a retirement remove a folder only when its pull request is merged, and told the maintainer. That changes the first of the three points above: a pull request closed without merging keeps its records until [issue #641](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/641)'s carry-over mark exists. Keeping them longer is the safe direction, and the maintainer may overrule it.

The tip keeps the records of every open pull request. It also keeps those of a pull request merged in the last 30 days, counted from `merged_at`, and those of every pull request closed without merging, until [issue #641](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/641)'s carry-over mark exists. Every other merged pull request's changeset is retired. Its records stay in the branch's history.

verification.reason: The finding holds as a mismatch between the new design.md text and the code. Line 364 says the tip keeps records of PRs "merged or closed in the last 30 days" and that `retire` removes "a finished pull request's changeset". In `retire`, a folder whose name is not in `merged` goes to `kept` unread (git-record-store.ts:288), and the retirement decision says `merged` holds only merged PRs. Closed-unmerged PRs are kept indefinitely until issue #641, not retired at 30 days (decision lines 15, 31, 54). So a closed PR's 40-day-old folder stays on the tip, as the scenario says. The code follows the decision, and the design.md sentence is the inaccurate part. The sentence is new at head, since the base has no such text. This is a documentation inaccuracy with no code defect, and the linked decision states the real rule.
